paragraphs.text: Craft is getting cheaper every quarter.
For most of my career, seniority showed up in the details: the tighter grid, the better easing curve, the screen you knew to cut. That was the job, and it was worth paying for.
It’s being automated from both ends. Agents
while they write UI, and the floor has risen so far that
a decent-looking design is now the baseline
. Give a model the same context you have and it can make the edit too. The better that context gets, the less a designer’s eye adds on its own.

What stays expensive is the work around the work: deciding which problem is worth solving, framing it so anyone, or anything, can start, and owning what happens after it ships. That isn’t a softer version of design. It’s the part we used to hand to product managers.
Senior design is moving upstream. Follow it, or get priced like a tool.
